question.problem:
Written in the form $y=mx+b,$ what is the equation of the line that passes through the points $(3,-10)$ and $(0,-4)?$

The equation of the line is $y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$ 

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-4-(-10)}{0-3} \\  & =\frac{-4+10}{0-3} \\  & =\frac{6}{-3} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

The coordinates of the $y$-intercept are always $(0,b).$ We know that the line passes through the point $(0,-4),$ so the $y$-intercept is $b=-4.$

Substituting the slope $m=-2$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-4$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-2x-4.
$$
